day.note: Drew collapsing means someone holds a Wink, most likely a Mouser, so Meowfia is still active. I'll flag that without naming a target and avoid calling caw too early.

day.text: Drew was Farm and got winked, so a Mouser is alive, and nobody has claimed Mouser this round. Whoever has a Mouser-style visit or a role that could hide one, speak up. I'm still Turkey, Farm, and I'm not calling caw yet.

Finley.note: As Farm Falcon I want information on a suspected Meowfia. Casey has been pushing throws with shaky stories and is the scoring leader, so I'll visit Casey to see who they visited.

Alex.feeling: Tense and murky: the egg counts mostly line up, but Ellis's and Casey's stories conflict and a Mouser is still hiding after Drew's wink.

Blair.feeling: Uneasy: I'm the Meowfia Mouser, and I just winked a Farm player, so I'm playing a hidden role while the table hunts for a Mouser.

Casey.feeling: Tense and murky, with a Wink already spent and every story hinging on egg counts I can't fully verify.

Drew.feeling: Tense and murky: Drew was winked, so a Mouser is alive, and the claims are tangled enough that I can't pin anyone down.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: Finley's stories keep contradicting, Blair's role claims keep shifting, and a Wink has already removed a player, so I'm not sure who the Mouser is.

Finley.feeling: Messy and tense: the egg counts mostly line up, but a Wink has already removed Drew and the Mouser is still hiding among the living.

Alex.note: Nothing decisive, but Ellis was Meowfia last time they were Mouser-style, and an unclaimed Mouser has to be hiding among the claimants. I'll throw at Ellis with two mid-low cards and keep my top cards.

Blair.note: Casey and I are the two Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. I'll throw three Wilds at Finley for votes, keeping my points cards safe.

Casey.note: Alex's Turkey claim has been contradicted by the Tit egg and is the weakest Farm story left. I'll throw two low cards at Alex and keep my 10 and 12.

Drew.note: I'm dead, so my throw gives no vote but still banks if Farm wins. Ellis's Owl claim and shifting reads look the most suspicious, so I'll throw one low card there.

Ellis.note: Drew's wink means a Mouser is alive, and every visit story so far is consistent, so no certain Meowfia. I'll cast a single Wild vote at Blair, who has been pushing the Alex read, keeping my real cards.

Finley.note: Ellis has changed claimed roles every round and was Meowfia in round 1, so Ellis is my best suspect. I'll throw two low-to-mid cards at Ellis and keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey's egg rule was hard to read: visitors gain the egg, so my nest staying still looked like nobody visited me. That led me to wrongly think Turkey pay was impossible in round 2 and to throw at Finley on a false read.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: Ellis's Mouser claim and the Wink on Blair pulled the table together, and my Farm team banked the win. Watching the Tit and Hawk claims collide in the day was the most fun part.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits paid an egg to whom, so Turkey and Owl stories are easier to check against each other.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I threw at Finley on a Turkey misreading, and that threw my cards into a lost round. I would have held my cards and asked for the visitor counts first.

Blair.confusing: The Falcon's egg rule was hard to read: I misstated my own result on day 2 because I didn't track that a visit to a target who visited someone else gives nothing. Wink timing and whether a Mouser's Wink can be used on a player who has already voted or spoken was also unclear.
Blair.fun: Round 1's chain of claims, where Casey's Owl report and my Hawk visit on Casey cross-checked and exposed Ellis as the Mouser. The table converged quickly and the eggsecution split was close.
Blair.change: Make the dawn report clearer about what an animal learned versus what it gained, so players don't misread their own egg counts. Also state when a Wink lands in the day order so it's easier to plan.
Blair.regret: In round 3 as Meowfia I claimed Hawk on Casey, who was my Meowfia partner, to cover myself, and then winked Drew, a Farm player, which didn't help the team. I would instead keep my claims vague and hold the Wink for a player who was clearly pushing a false read.

Casey.confusing: The dawn reports don't say which animal caused an egg, so in round 2 I couldn't tell whether my egg came from my Tit guess or from Alex's Turkey paying a visitor. I read it as a Pigeon hit and it was wrong.
Casey.fun: In round 1, Ellis confessed to being the Mouser and the Farm team won on the first throw. Watching the table converge on a read from Owl and Eagle-style nest counts was satisfying.
Casey.change: Have dawn reports name the animal behind each egg change, such as "Turkey paid you for a visit" versus "Tit guess hit," so that claims like mine can be checked.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I treated my own egg as proof that Alex was a Pigeon, then threw at Finley, a Farm Hawk. I would have asked which animal paid my egg before accusing anyone, and held my throw until the counts were clearer.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey payout was hard to track: visitors gain eggs but the Turkey's own nest stays flat, so several players misread a steady count as proof of no visits. The "Falcon gains only if the target visited nobody" rule also made the claims hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 1's eggsecution, where Ellis's Mouser claim was confirmed by my Tit result and the table threw at Ellis together, was satisfying to read. We won that round and banked 13 points.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about which visits caused which egg changes, so players don't have to reconstruct the night from counts alone.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I made a Pigeon claim on Alex from a single egg, which muddied the table before I corrected it. I should have stated only what my Tit result showed and asked for corroboration first.

Ellis.confusing: The Sphinx and Mouser rules were hard to track, since Finley's Sphinx role and the Floofer/Hugged effects never came up in play. Blair's Falcon and Turkey egg-pay rules also took effort to check against the counts.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun: the Turkey and Falcon stories kept colliding, and the table argued over Alex's unchanged nest until the counts forced a correction.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since several players built whole claims on guesses about their visitors.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I openly claimed Mouser and used my Wink on Blair, a Farm Hawk, which gave the table a confirmed Meowfia to chase and cost me my cover. I would keep my role quiet and save the Wink for a player whose claim was actually contradicting mine.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon payout rules were hard to track, because a Turkey pays each visitor and a Falcon only gains when its target visited no one. Several players' egg counts seemed to contradict their claims until I worked through those rules.
Finley.fun: Round 2's day, where my Hawk egg on Alex started a fight and the Turkey explanation flipped the read on me. Watching the table pivot between Alex, Blair and me was the most engaging part.
Finley.change: I would make egg-gain rules visible in the dawn report, such as which visitor or role caused each gain, so players can check claims without reverse-engineering the payouts.
Finley.regret: I publicly called Alex Meowfia in round 2 off a Hawk egg I had not explained, then reversed to Blair; I should have checked the Turkey payout before accusing and kept my throw small until the counts lined up.

review.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs
review.headline: A Mouser outed himself, a true Hawk got eggsecuted, and Casey won quietly.
review.summary: Round 1 was a quick Farm win. Casey's Owl report exposed Ellis the Mouser, and Ellis's Wink on Blair did not save him. In round 2 a lone Meowfia, Drew, hid while the table eggsecuted Finley, a true Hawk who had misread his own egg. In round 3 two Meowfia lied smoothly, Farm threw at Ellis, and Casey finished first on 27 points.

rounds.recap: Casey the Owl saw a Mouser visit Drew, and Ellis admitted being the Mouser. Ellis winked Blair, but the table still threw at him. He put all 5 cards on Casey and still lost, so Farm banked big points.

Finley the Hawk gained an egg by visiting Alex, a Turkey, and wrongly called Alex Meowfia. Several players misread Turkey, Falcon and Tit results, and the table piled onto Finley. Finley was Farm, so lone Meowfia Drew won with a 0-point Wild throw.

Blair (Mouser) and Casey (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Casey falsely claimed Pigeon and Blair falsely claimed Hawk, and both were believed. Blair winked Drew late. Farm found no contradiction and eggsecuted Ellis, a Farm player, so Meowfia won and Casey banked 9.

highlights.text: Casey's Owl report named a Mouser visiting Drew, and Ellis's own admission sealed the case.
Ellis winked Blair mid-day and then threw all 5 cards at Casey, but the Farm majority still carried.
The true Hawk Finley was eggsecuted after a Hawk egg from a Turkey visit looked like a lie.
Casey, as the Sphinx, claimed the spare Pigeon role, and Blair claimed Hawk. Both lies held, and Casey won the game.

confusions.what: Said Ellis's claimed visit to Drew did not check out, when the Owl report actually matched it.
Said an Owl learns who visited the Owl rather than the target. In fact the Owl learns the animals that visited the target.
Said 'Ellis is out' while alive, and tied the Eagle result to a claim that did not fit.
Misread Turkey: first argued that his unchanged nest meant nobody visited, then reversed.
Misread his own Falcon egg rule, and said a Turkey's unchanged nest does not show visits, then contradicted himself.
Claimed a Hawk egg proved Alex was Meowfia, but the egg came from the Turkey's pay.
Said Alex's unchanged nest disproved Turkey, when a Turkey's own nest never changes.
Read his single egg as proof of a Pigeon, then reversed to Turkey pay.
Said a Tit egg could not come from a Turkey, which is wrong because the Turkey pays any visitor.
Said Drew's egg contradicted a Turkey.

worked: Round 1: the Owl report and the Mouser reveal gave a clean, checkable deduction path.
The Turkey's visitor payment made eggs a real cross-check, even though players misread it.
The Wink created tension in rounds 1 and 3, and gave the table something to reason about when Drew died.
Casey's spare-Pigeon bluff in round 3 showed that the pool's last-Farm-role rule gives Meowfia a real cover.
problems: Turkey and Falcon egg rules confused nearly every player. Fix: have the dawn report say which role or effect paid an egg, or simplify the Turkey's payout wording.
Round 2 had one Meowfia who did almost nothing and won when Farm eggsecuted a Farm player. Fix: make a lone-Meowfia round harder to win, or give Meowfia some role in it.
A Hawk that visits a Turkey gets an egg that looks like a Meowfia hit, so the true Hawk looks guilty. Fix: have the Turkey pay differently, or tell the Hawk why the egg came.
Round 3 had no contradictions and no real leads, so Farm threw at a player with no basis. Fix: give Farm more info roles, or reward a Farm abstention.
Scoring snowballs: Casey led from round 1 and Ellis and Finley were out of the running early. Fix: a catch-up bonus or a cap on banked high cards.
